newsitem.title: ITALY: Call to try Priebke in Italy civil court rejected.
newsitem.headline: Call to try Priebke in Italy civil court rejected.

text.p: A military court trying former Nazi SS officers Erich Priebke and Karl Hass for their role in Italy's worst World War Two atrocity threw out a request by local Jews on Thursday to move the trial to a civilian court.

The military tribunal rejected claims by lawyers representing Rome's Jewish Community that Priebke and Hass -- who are accused of complicity in the 1944 massacre of 335 men and boys -- should be tried for genocide, which is punishable under Italy's penal, not military, code.
In a separate decision on Thursday, a Rome appeals court turned down a call from Hass' lawyers to set the 84-year-old free from house arrest during the course of the trial.

The change-of-venue request by the Jewish Community, a civil plaintiff in the trial, had been opposed by both defence lawyers on the grounds that genocide did not exist as a crime in Italy at the time of the massacre.
Prosecutors had also been opposed, arguing that Italy's high court had already decided on the military trial.
After the ruling, military prosecutor Antonino Intelisano began laying out his case against Priebke and Hass.

"The role of the defendants was not only in the dark and sinister execution of an order given by a superior. It was in the voluntary execution of an illegitimate order," Intelisano told the court in his opening statements.

Priebke's defense lawyer Carlo Taormina told reporters after Thursday's session that he will ask for all of the charges against his client to be dropped by contesting the extradition request which in 1995 brought Priebke from Argentina to Italy.
Priebke and Hass have admitted to taking part in the massacre at Rome's Ardeatine Caves but claim they were forced to follow orders or face the firing squad themselves.
Seventy-five of the victims, rounded up and shot in reprisal for a partisan bomb attack on Nazi occupying forces, were Jews.
Priebke, 83, is being tried for the second time in the case after a controversial "guilty but not punishable" verdict at the end of his first trial last August was quashed on appeal.
The latest trial, at which Hass is a co-defendant for the first time, opened last week in the fortified courtroom of Rome's high-security Rebibbia jail.
Priebke being held under house arrest at a Roman Catholic monastery south of Rome.
